newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares ended mixed to lower with some profit-taking halting the market's recent rise as investors digested the continuing stream of earnings reports.
The AEX index of 25 blue chip shares closed 3.36 points or 0.45 percent lower at 747.15 and dealers said the index faced pretty stiff resistance around the 750 mark now.
A 20-basis-point rise in the Dutch central bank's special advances rate came half an hour before the market closed and was bigger than the 10 basis points generally expected.
Most dealers viewed the hike as a response to recent guilder weakness against the mark and saw no reason to become bearish.
"Sure, a rate hike is a negative but in my view this is purely a currency story and we don't have to worry about it too much," said one dealer.
Others agreed with this, saying Dutch money market rates had to rise closer to those in Germany to counter recent softness of the guilder which is normally dead steady against the mark.
Two big blue chips, bank ABN AMRO and chemicals group Akzo Nobel, both succumbed to profit-taking after reporting 1996 results right in line with market expectations.
ABN AMRO was off 2.40 guilders at 140.00 while Akzo Nobel shed 4.10 at 279.00.
Defensive stocks such as Unilever and Royal Dutch also lost ground to profit-taking, closing 4.80 and 4.10 guilders lower at 370.70 and 332.50 respectively.

But Gist-Brocades, which reported a 10 percent rise in 1996 net profit on Wednesday, continued its recent advance, closing 3.00 guilders firmer at 65.20 and bringing its cumulative rise over the last three sessions to 8.20 guilders.
